text: With "Start Minimized" and "Fullscreen" this is the classic cast-target setup: the app waits out of the way, plays fullscreen when something casts to it, and goes back to waiting when the
video ends or you press Q.
Requires restart to change. MPV keybinds are used by default. Press ENTER to drive the player controls by keyboard. "No player controls" leaves playback bare; the library, the keyboard
shortcuts and the menu key still work.
Always Bind Arrow Keys to Player Controls
The controls have to stay legible over any frame. "None" gives the text a drop shadow instead of shading the picture behind it.
"Hide unless hovered" keeps them up only while the pointer is on them, paused or not.
0 hides them as soon as the pointer is not on them, and forces "Hide unless hovered".
During playback only — in the library those buttons stay Back and Forward. Off by default because they are easy to hit by accident on some mice. Takes effect after a restart.
Show What You're Watching in Discord
Discord Rich Presence. Takes effect after a restart.
Palette, glow, cover style and default cover size. Colours change immediately; cover and heading sizes take effect after a restart.
Overrides the theme's cover size. Applies immediately, and is also on the View menu of any library.
Takes effect after a restart. "Follow display" uses the scale your desktop reports, which is 100% on X11.
Leave this to Default unless setting up passthrough. Note some audio servers like Pipewire don't like passthrough and will need to be disabled for a card before it'll let *any* audio through in
passthrough mode. In my tests I got silence otherwise, but results may vary.
"Default" changes nothing and lets MPV (and your own mpv.conf) decide. Pick a mode only if you are sending audio to a receiver.
Evens out loud effects and quiet dialogue. This turns passthrough off while it is enabled, because the volume has to be adjusted before your receiver gets the audio.
"hq" offers heavier profiles. Pick it if you have a fast graphics card.
Leave on Automatic unless video breaks when a profile is loaded. This only applies while a profile is active, and OpenGL can cost you HDR output.
Pixels one wheel notch scrolls. On a grid this is rounded so a whole number of notches spans one row, whichever scroll mode you are in — a trackpad or trackball never leaves you a sliver of a
row off. Raise it to scroll faster, lower it for finer control.
"Continuous" scrolls by pixels and lands wherever the wheel puts it; it lines rows up by itself if the display cannot keep up. Pick "Aligned to rows" if scrolling still stutters — on a very large
display, a slow or remote one, or with an external MPV. Pick "One row per notch" to move a whole row (or one home-screen section) at a time.
Page the library and music tile grids instead of scrolling: each page is one screenful with First / Previous / Next / Last controls and a page number you can type into. Easier than precise
Make Live TV logos more legible
Channel logos come as ink on a transparent background, drawn for the white page other clients put them on — so on a dark one the black ones vanish. On, they are backed with the light plate
they were made for, and the few whose own outline is white get a drop shadow so they still have an edge against it. Off, they get the theme's card colour and no shadows, as Jellyfin Web
The same treatment for a library set to draw Logo artwork. Off by default, because a film's or series' logo is white by convention and already reads on a dark background — the plate is what
makes it need a shadow. Turn it on if yours are dark.
Applies to srv1, enable other servers in servers tab.
Some changes take effect after restarting.
